description: Agent Reliability: submit a service’s maintenance record for a period with its maintenance policy: the record with the service, the period, whether maintenance time was counted or excluded in the period’s uptime figures, and each window with its id, when it was announced, when it started and ended or its minutes; the policy with the service, the least notice in hours, the longest window in minutes, the most windows a calendar month may hold and whether maintenance time counts in uptime. The signed report gives the record and the policy, each window’s notice in hours and length in minutes, the windows each month holds, and the uptime treatment as each document states it, and counts them, and names a divergent record: a window announced with less notice than the policy requires, a window longer than it allows, a month with more windows than it allows and maintenance time excluded from uptime where the policy counts it; then maintenance counted where the policy excludes it, windows outside the period and another service, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No notice, longest window or monthly limit in the policy, the treatment unstated on either side, or a window with no announcement time or no length leaves the record unverified. Notice reads from times of day, lengths compare to the tenth of a minute and frequency counts by the day each window starts. A maintenance record is read against the policy behind it: wever_sla-credit-check works out one month’s uptime with scheduled maintenance set apart where the terms exclude it and names the credit, and wever_sla-evidence-check restates one SLA’s exclusions and notice terms on their own, while the maintenance check computes no uptime or credit and reads each window’s notice, length and frequency and the uptime treatment against the policy. Verdict rely_maintenance_divergent, rely_maintenance_partial, rely_maintenance_unverified or rely_maintenance_consistent. POST /api/rely-maintenance-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
